memoryText: He has told you, O man, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Micah 6:8 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse has been called the whole of religion in a sentence. It follows a series of absurd questions: how many sacrifices would be enough? Micah cuts through them. “He has told you.” God’s will is not hidden. It is not a puzzle for experts. It has been spoken clearly, and it is simple, though not easy.

“To do justice.” Justice is not an idea to hold but a thing to do. It means setting right what is wrong, especially for those who have no power to defend themselves. It is the opposite of the land-grabbing and bribe-taking that Micah condemned.

“To love kindness.” The word is hesed, covenant loyalty and mercy. We are not only to practice kindness but to love it, to delight in being merciful, as God delights in showing mercy. It is the difference between a duty performed and a joy shared.

“To walk humbly with your God.” The image is of a companion on a journey. We walk with God, not ahead of him or away from him. Humility means we know we are dependent on his grace, that we did not earn our place beside him.

This verse does not replace the gospel. It describes the life of those who have received it. We cannot do any of these three things by our own power. Jesus did them perfectly in our place, and through his Spirit he now enables us to follow him. Say this verse as a prayer for the week ahead.
weekInReview: This week you finished the book of Jonah and learned that God’s mercy extends even to Nineveh, and that the prophet who was rescued from the deep was angry at the mercy shown to others. You read Micah, the prophet from a small village, who spoke against land-grabbing, corrupt leaders, and false prophets, and who promised a ruler from tiny Bethlehem who would be the peace of his people. You read the lawsuit of chapter 6 and its great summary of what God requires, and the closing hymn to the God who casts our sins into the depths of the sea. And you read the account of the fall of Samaria in 2 Kings, with its sober explanation: they would not listen. The week taught that God asks for justice, kindness, and humble faith, and that he delights to pardon.
reflectionQuestions: Jonah was angry that God showed mercy to Nineveh. Is there anyone whose forgiveness you find hard to accept?
Micah promises that a ruler will come from little Bethlehem, and that “he shall be their peace.” How has Christ been your peace?
Micah 6:8 names three things: do justice, love kindness, walk humbly. Which one do you most need to grow in this week, and what is one step you can take?
prayerPrompts: Tell God what doing justice, loving kindness, and walking humbly will look like for you.
Thank Jesus, who is our peace and casts sins into the depths of the sea.
